_comment: ONE roster, fed through BOTH config readers — the desk-tools deskkit reader
and statusgen — with identical expected verdicts. This file is the cross-tree
binding that replaced the textual KEEP-IN-SYNC grep when the trust roster
Each module reads its own copy of this shared vector file.
The two modules deliberately share no code, so a shared VECTOR file is what
keeps their duplicated readers honest: a drift in either reader fails here.
The identities are deliberately NOT this house's — the roster is adopter
configuration now, and a fixture that only works with one organisation's
EXTENDED at review (correctness finding 3). The vector originally carried
only the three TRUST variables, so the repo-policy parse sat structurally outside the
binding that is supposed to keep the duplicated readers honest — and the two copies had
in fact diverged on it: deskkit validated the ci|no-ci / public|private tokens and
collapsed the whole configuration on a bad one, while statusgen stored the token
unvalidated and reported configured=true. One file, one typo, opposite verdicts.
So the vector now carries the ALLOWED-REPO set and the ROLE bindings as well, and a
list of rosters BOTH readers must REFUSE. A refusal case is what actually binds the
validation halves: an acceptance case only proves the two agree on a good file.

cases.why: the blessing authority: trusted, id-verified, and the ONE identity that may bless
the blessing authority carrying a RECYCLED id: login matches, id does not (P4)
a second trusted human is a trusted AUTHOR but may NEVER bless
a trusted human with the wrong id is untrusted CONTENT (recycled-login defence)
a human with NO numeric id on a surface that has one: id 0 means the surface lacks it, and a human without one fails the strict content check
cases.whyAuthorID: the ONE delta from trustedContent: a human with no numeric id is login-only on the GENERAL-PURPOSE path, which exists for surfaces (gh CLI list JSON) that structurally carry no id. The strict content path fails closed on the same input

cases.why: a configured App in the REST rendering — trusted author and trusted content, never a blessing authority
the same App in the gh CLI rendering — both renderings are accepted
Apps are trusted by login alone even with no id (an App cannot be recycled)
the BARE slug is never trusted: slugs and usernames are separate GitHub namespaces, so a plain user could squat one
case is insignificant — GitHub logins are case-insensitively unique, so a case variant is the same account
an empty login is untrusted, never a wildcard
a near-miss on the blessing authority's login must not bless
the blessing authority's login rendered as an App must not bless (or be trusted at all)

an UNPINNED configured human on a surface that HAS an id: trusted author, but untrusted content — nothing to check the id against, so pinning is what buys trust on an id-bearing surface (this case was missing, which is how the two readers diverged on it)
cases.whyAuthorID: MUTATION A. An UNPINNED configured human on an id-bearing surface: there is nothing to compare the id against, so pinning is what buys trust. The conversion briefly made this `want == 0 => trusted`, i.e. trusted carrying ANY id — the exact login-recycling exposure P4 closes, and a WIDENING against the pre-conversion `return ok && want == id`. This case is the one that reddens on it

cases.why: the same unpinned human on a surface with NO id: login-only, as before the conversion
cases.whyAuthorID: the same unpinned human on a surface with NO id: login-only, as before the conversion — the general-purpose path must NOT be tightened here either, or gh-CLI-sourced surfaces stop trusting a configured identity

repoCases.why: an explicitly configured repo: allowed, CI required, private
public visibility is honoured when stated (it risk-classes unconditionally, #382)
UNSTATED policy takes the fail-closed defaults: CI REQUIRED, visibility UNKNOWN. Mutations M11/M12 flipped exactly these two and survived the old suite
a repo outside the configured set is refused — the write boundary is a whitelist
an attacker-owned lookalike of a configured name is refused

roleCases.why: a role bound by the role= prefix resolves to the App's REST rendering
a role NOT bound by any prefix must refuse, never answer an empty login a caller could compare against

rejectedRosters.why: a one-character typo in a repo POLICY token. deskkit refused the whole configuration; statusgen accepted it — the divergence this list exists to bind
a repo entry that is not an owner/name slug
a typo'd key in the ASSAY_ namespace. The surface it meant to configure stays EMPTY while the configuration would otherwise report itself correct
rejectedRosters.problemContains: unknown key in the ASSAY_ namespace

rejectedRosters.why: the blessing authority carrying no numeric id — mandatory on this surface alone
the blessing authority given as a LIST — never the first entry, never every entry
a schema version this build does not speak

the blessing authority is ALSO a configured App. The looksLikeBot arm does NOT catch this slug — 'helios' carries no [bot]/app/ affix and no -app/-bot suffix — so the inBotSet arm is the only thing standing between an App and the authority that admits external text into the desks' own queues. Both readers carry that arm; a mutation disabling it in either survived the whole suite before this case existed.
rejectedRosters.problemContains: must never be the blessing authority
